body: Worker rule (Termal::BarA2, 2026-10-28 17:27Z; my own slip while preparing a B16 slice). Never run a shell command with another session's worktree as the working directory, or aimed at it with `git -C`. That includes read-only commands like `sed`, `cat` or `git status`. Its runs may be in progress, and a command from another writable session in that worktree can refuse their credit; git status can even refresh the index. To read someone else's root, use only the Read and Grep tools, which run no commands there. If a command does land there, tell the coordinator and that session at once, naming the commands and their times.
